subject: SLO check: private inference egress & streaming latency (FinWise)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Moss <lena.moss@finwise.com>, ops+infra@finwise.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: SLO check: private inference egress & streaming latency (FinWise)

Hi Lena / FinWise infra team —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and the concrete asks so we can line up a short network verification window next week. High-level goal: validate end-to-end streaming token latency and sustained throughput from your VPC -> Redwood Private (peered/VPN) for the PoC.

Target acceptance numbers (proposed):
- Streaming token latency (end-to-end): p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 250ms (measured per-token at 1kb prompt sizes)
- Request throughput: sustained 250 req/s for 5m windows, burst to 750 req/s for 30s
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent sessions with ~8 tokens/sec average output per session
- Egress bandwidth observed: expect ~300–700 Mbps depending on model/quantization

What we need from you to schedule the test run:
1) Confirm whether traffic will egress via the peered VPC or site-to-site VPN (NAT details if any).
2) If peered, please share the peering/router public endpoints and any firewall rules that might shape UDP/TCP (we use both TCP for control and occasional UDP perf probes).
3) MTU and MSS settings on the path; any forced TCP window limits or proxy layers.
4) Point person and a 90-minute window (we propose Apr 6–7 mornings PT).

Ben and Aditya: attaching our lightweight SLO template and an example PoC topology (PNG). Ben, please add anything I missed on the measurement suite.

Next steps: once we get 1–3 above, Redwood will provision a temporary test harness in your peered subnet and run: traceroute + pktsize sweep, iperf3 baseline, and a streaming token-emulation run using our harness (links in related_links). We’ll capture token-level timing and a packet-level capture where you permit it.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales (Networking)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-network-slo-template.pdf, finwise-poc-topology.png

From: Lena Moss <lena.moss@finwise.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+infra@finwise.com
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO check: private inference egress & streaming latency (FinWise)

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear checklist. Quick responses from FinWise infra:

- We can do site-to-site VPN peering initially (IPsec) and are open to switching to cloud peering after the PoC. We will NAT the outbound traffic to a known egress IP (ops+infra will share).
- MTU on our side is 1450; there is an L4 load balancer in front of the infra that may terminate connections — we can open a bypass path for the test to avoid additional proxying.
- We probably can hit the p99 target you proposed but need the empirical run to be sure; our initial internal goal is p95 < 150ms.

ops+infra will be the technical owner for the test window — we propose Thu Apr 6 09:30–11:00 PT. If that works for Redwood, we’ll reserve it and send the peering details.

Lena Moss
Head of Platform Engineering
FinWise

On Wed, Apr 4, 2028 at 09:45 AM ops+infra@finwise.com wrote:
> Ops note: will share egress IPs and firewall ACL by EOD. We prefer no packet capture saved offsite; can provide tcpdump output for diagnostic review.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Moss <lena.moss@finwise.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+infra@finwise.com
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 07:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO check: private inference egress & streaming latency (FinWise)

Appreciate the details — a few technical clarifications from Redwood infra/serving:

- Traceroute and iperf are great as a baseline. For the streaming token timing we need: round-trip ICMP + TCP SYN->ACK timing, and a small HTTP streaming test where we push a canonical 1k prompt and measure server-to-client token times (we’ll provide the harness container).
- Important: ensure that any L4 load balancer isn’t doing HTTP/2 multiplexing or request coalescing during the test; that will skew per-token timing. If bypassing LB is feasible for the test window, please do that.
- Please confirm whether your VPN will NAT source ports (we rely on stable source ports for some of our streaming RTCP-style probes).
- If packet capture cannot leave your environment, we can accept locally-stored pcap files and a short script that extracts our required timing fields.

Suggested test steps (we’ll run these on our side once peering details are provided):
1) baseline iperf3 (5m) to measure throughput and jitter;
2) traceroutes (UDP/TCP) to pick up routing asymmetry;
3) small-scale streaming run: 10 concurrent sessions, 8 tokens/s avg, 1 minute;
4) scale to 50 concurrent sessions for a 5-minute sustained run;
5) capture p50/p95/p99 token timing and packet-level retransmit counts.

We’ll bring a fallback plan if we see consistent p99 spikes: enable local prefix caching and reduce concurrency on the initial rollout.

Ben Carter
Technical Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Moss <lena.moss@finwise.com>, ops+infra@finwise.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO check: private inference egress & streaming latency (FinWise)

Perfect — thanks everyone. Confirming the test window: Thu Apr 6, 09:30–11:00 PT. Owners and responsibilities:
- FinWise ops (ops+infra): share egress IPs, firewall ACL, and note on packet-capture constraints (owner: ops+infra).
- Redwood (Ben): provide the harness container, test scripts, and a small results extraction script.
- Redwood (Aditya): coordinate infra account access and ephemeral credentials during the window.
- Kimberly: overall PoC coordinator; will run the acceptance checklist and file a short results summary within 24h of the test.

Deliverables for the test:
- Short README (how to run the harness)
- iperf/traceroute outputs + streaming timing CSVs
- Pass/fail against the proposed SLOs above and recommended mitigations if we see p99 artifacts

I’ve attached the SLO template and topology again for reference. If anything changes on your side, please flag immediately. Looking forward to the run.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales (Networking)
Redwood Inference
